best_for: Solo users and small teams who want Notion-style docs, wikis and kanban boards in an AGPL desktop app, and who can live with a 100 MB cloud limit or pay per member.
description:
AppFlowy is a workspace app from AppFlowy-IO, built with Flutter and Rust. Its makers say they used Notion every day on a paid plan, and started AppFlowy because of what they saw as Notion's weak spots in data security and on phones.

You can run a small project, keep a basic customer list, or build a simple website with the site builder. Forms collect answers straight into your workspace. The AI tools can search your pages, help you write, answer questions in a chat and take meeting notes. If your language is missing, you can add a translation yourself through the project's online translation editor.

points.title: Docs, databases and boards
points.text: AppFlowy covers block-based documents, team wikis, kanban boards and databases whose rows open as pages with comments. If you know Notion, the layout will feel familiar.

points.title: Free Personal plan has tight limits
points.text: The Personal plan costs nothing but has one workspace owner, 100 MB of storage, files up to 7 MB, 7 days of version history, one form, one chart and a limited AI trial. It suits notes and plans more than a shared file library.

points.title: Pro is priced per member
points.text: Pro is USD 12 per member per month billed yearly, or USD 16 billed monthly. It removes the storage and upload caps, keeps 90 days of history and allows unlimited guest editors at no charge. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Self-hosting is no longer fully open
points.text: The app is AGPL-3.0, but the current self-hosted server is a closed commercial codebase. Its free tier gives one user seat per instance plus up to 3 guest editors. The old open-source server repo is archived and no longer maintained.

points.title: Moving in from Notion
points.text: Export your Notion workspace as a zip and upload it on AppFlowy's import page. It lands in a new workspace named after the zip, and you get an email when it is done. Big workspaces export faster without files and images.

points.title: Linux and phones are elsewhere
points.text: This site lists Windows and macOS only. AppFlowy's own download page also offers a Linux AppImage, and there are iPhone and Android apps in their stores.

points.title: Versions kept on this site
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 105 versions of the 64-bit, machine-wide installer. macOS gets a universal build for Intel and Apple Silicon, macOS 12 or later, but lists only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
